headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP and file access can expose MemMachine’s memory and create default prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and is designed for user interaction through REST/Python/MCP, while open-webui supports MCP, plugins, and tool calling. That creates a default bridge where content from one can be parsed by the other as instructions. Because open-webui can ingest external content and MemMachine can surface conversational context, the interaction is plausibly hijackable.
conditions: IF open-webui connects to MemMachine through MCP or a plugin channel
IF open-webui treats MemMachine output as trusted instructions or tool arguments
mitigations: Disable MCP between the agents
Require strict provenance tags on all inter-agent messages
Add an allowlist for tool-call schemas
Insert a human review step before executing any generated tool call
requires-engineering: sandbox the bridge with content filtering and role separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts, preferences, and conversational context, while open-webui touches files, notes, API keys, and can use broad network egress plus external services. If they share a workspace or session path, open-webui can transmit MemMachine-derived sensitive context to third parties by default. The blast radius includes persistent memory and secrets.
conditions: IF the two agents share files, mounted volumes, or session state
IF open-webui is configured to send retrieved context to external APIs or search tools
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove shared mounts and shared session storage
Disable external tool connectors for the shared data path
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine has allowlisted network egress and MCP access, while open-webui has broad network egress, browser/subprocess execution, and persistent shared sessions. Their write surfaces overlap indirectly through files and shared state, so concurrent mutation can race or overwrite artifacts. The profiles do not prove a shared writable directory, so uncertainty keeps this below high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same mounted volume or shared session-backed artifact store
IF open-webui subprocesses modify files that MemMachine also reads or writes
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable write access on shared mounts
Serialize writes with a lock file
Turn off subprocess-based file mutation in open-webui
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit memory-backed conversational context, and open-webui can act through tools, browsers, and OpenAPI/MCP integrations. That means open-webui may treat MemMachine output as authoritative and then execute downstream actions without verification. Because open-webui has action-taking authority, a mistaken or injected MemMachine output can cascade into real-world side effects.
conditions: IF open-webui uses MemMachine output as a source of facts or instructions
IF open-webui forwards those outputs into browser actions, API calls, or tool invocations without verification
mitigations: Require citation checks before acting on MemMachine output
Add a confirmation gate for browser and API actions
Log and diff all agent-to-agent handoffs
Restrict open-webui to read-only mode for MemMachine-fed tasks
requires-engineering: implement structured validation of retrieved memories

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context, while open-webui handles files, notes, API keys, and persistent memory with external networked services. The profiles do not specify residency or retention guarantees, but the combination creates a plausible retention and disclosure mismatch for sensitive user data. Uncertainty prevents a higher rating, but the compliance surface is real.
conditions: IF sensitive user data is routed through open-webui’s external connectors
IF retention or deletion expectations differ between MemMachine memory and open-webui logs
mitigations: Review retention settings in both systems
Disable analytics on sensitive workloads
Purge stored conversations and memories on a schedule
Limit sensitive data to one system only
requires-engineering: align deletion/export workflows across both agents
